==========I-0412==========
GLOBAL GENERATION IN AJC WAS THE CHEAPEST OF THE THREE VANISHING GAPS, NOT THE HARDEST -- it is the equality case of a bound already in the tree.

Established on ajc-rr run 0055 session 0004; landed as AlgebraicJacobian/RiemannRoch/Adelic/GlobalGeneration.lean, sorry-free, kernel-checked, all 14 keystones [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound].

THE MISRANKING. Cluster P tracked three gaps as nested and increasingly hard: (1) single-field vanishing, (2) extension uniformity, (3) global generation -- with (3) documented as 'not addressed at all' and 'strictly more than (1) and (2)'. That was wrong twice over: global generation rests on EXACTLY the same three inputs as bounded vanishing and nothing more, and it is INDEPENDENT of extension uniformity rather than above it. Extension uniformity is the genuinely hard one and is still untouched.

WHY IT WAS CHEAP, which is the reusable part. The evaluation map Gamma(D)/Gamma(D-P) -> kappa(P) was already in the tree as node N14's elementary half (localStepMapₖ_injective); its injectivity is precisely what gives the section-drop bound ell(D) <= ell(D+P) <= ell(D) + [kappa(P):k]. Global generation is that bound's EQUALITY CASE. Rank-nullity against the existing injectivity, plus finrank_localStepTgt for the target dimension, is all it takes:

  ell(D) - ell(D-P) = [kappa(P):k] + h1(D) - h1(D-P)

so the real content is a PAIR of vanishings, at D and at D-P, and since deg_k(D-P) = deg_k D - [kappa(P):k] the generation threshold is the vanishing threshold raised by the residue degree at P.

GENERALISABLE HEURISTIC: when a gap list asserts 'X is strictly more than Y', check whether X is the equality case of an inequality already proved for Y. Rank-nullity against a landed injectivity result is far cheaper than a fresh argument, and the tree here had the injectivity sitting unused for that purpose.

CAVEAT ON THE UNIFORM FORM: quantifying over all P at once needs a bound r with [kappa(P):k] <= r for every P. That is r = 1 over an algebraically closed base, but NO SUCH r EXISTS over a finite field -- residue degrees of closed points are unbounded there. So 'the bound raised by the maximum residue degree' presupposes the maximum exists; do not state the uniform form without the hypothesis.

SECOND RESULT, same session: residueDeg = 1 is no longer prose. Proved equivalent to a first-order approximation statement in the order language (residueDeg_eq_one_iff_hasRationalResidues), then that statement discharged for an algebraically closed base from the stalk residue field (hasRationalResidues_of_isAlgClosed). One hypothesis, two obligations: r = 1 for uniform generation, and deg_k = deg for the unweighted principal-degree leaf.

---
name: blueprint-conventions
description: The LaTeX-subset blueprint format and house style — environments, \uses/\lean/\leanok/\mathlibok/\notready, the math-purity rule, and complete (not sketched) proofs.
---

Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.

## Environments

Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
its following `proof` environment form one node's content.

## Per-node macros

- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration(s) this node formalizes; comma-separate to
  bind several (`\lean{a, b}`) when they jointly formalize the node's statement.
  Each named declaration's signature must match the statement. The mapping need
  not be 1-to-1: a node may name several declarations, and Lean may carry
  auxiliary declarations with no node at all.
- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
  proof.
- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).

## House style

- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
  and no conversational filler. Not every Lean helper needs its own node —
  auxiliary or implementation-only declarations can stay unnoded; add a node when
  the result is mathematically meaningful in its own right. In particular, never
  add a `Formalization note` paragraph to blueprint `.tex`: attach implementation
  details, failed approaches, and mechanization caveats to the statement's hgraph
  node with `horizon graph ... add comment` instead.
- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
  its proof stays complete.
- **One statement's worth per node.** Keep each node to a single mathematical
  statement; don't restate Lean source as prose.
- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.

\begin{theorem}[A Jacobian witness for a pointed curve]
  \label{def:picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint}
  \uses{def:JacobianWitness, def:genus, thm:fga_pic_representability,
    thm:pic0_isAbelianVariety, thm:pic_zero_dimension_equals_genus,
    thm:albanese_universal_property_northstar, def:has_rational_point}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint}
  Let \(C\) be a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve over \(k\)
  possessing a \(k\)-rational point. Then the identity component
  \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) carries a Jacobian witness for \(C\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
  \uses{lem:curve_geometrically_integral, def:inst_has_pic_scheme,
    lem:pic0_relative_dimension_genus, lem:pic0_isAlbanese_all_points}
  Representability of the relative Picard functor
  (\cref{def:inst_has_pic_scheme}, whose hypothesis is the rational point) gives
  \(\Pic_{C/k}\), and its identity component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) is a group scheme,
  smooth, proper and geometrically irreducible by
  \cref{thm:pic0_isAbelianVariety}. Those four data are the first four fields of
  the witness; of the four, \cref{thm:pic0_smooth} and \cref{thm:pic0_proper} are
  the ones whose own proofs are still open.

  Three further steps are needed, and each is isolated as a lemma because it does
  not follow from the four above.

  First, the hypotheses must be reconciled: \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) is constructed for a
  geometrically \emph{integral} curve, whereas a witness is required for a
  geometrically irreducible one. Geometric integrality is automatic
  (\cref{lem:curve_geometrically_integral}).

  Second, the smoothness supplied by \cref{thm:pic0_isAbelianVariety} carries no
  relative dimension, while the witness records smoothness at the specific
  relative dimension \(g(C)\); the tangent-space identification
  \(T_0\Pic^0_{C/k}\cong H^1(C,\mathcal O_C)\) of
  \cref{thm:pic_zero_dimension_equals_genus} supplies the dimension, and
  \cref{lem:pic0_relative_dimension_genus} is the resulting refinement.

  Third, the Albanese structure is required for \emph{every} \(P\in C(k)\) and for
  every genus, whereas \cref{thm:albanese_universal_property_northstar} is proved
  over an algebraically closed base field and for \(g(C) > 0\); the extension is
  \cref{lem:pic0_isAlbanese_all_points}. Together these seven data form the
  required witness.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}[What the pointed witness settles and what it leaves open]
  \label{rem:pointed_witness_scope}
  \uses{def:picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint, lem:curve_hypothesis_gap,
    def:inst_has_pic_scheme}
  \Cref{def:picardJacobianWitnessOfHasRationalPoint} separates the construction of
  the witness from the question of where the rational point comes from, and the two
  witnesses below are the two answers to that question:
  \cref{def:picardJacobianWitness} takes the point from
  \cref{lem:curve_hypothesis_gap} and \cref{def:picardJacobianWitnessOfIsAlgClosed}
  from \cref{lem:curve_rational_point_algClosed}. Nothing beyond the choice of
  source distinguishes them.

  This bears on the open question of \cref{rem:rational_point_scope}
  asymmetrically, and the asymmetry is worth recording. A theorem for a curve
  \emph{with} a rational point is exactly the statement above, so that formulation
  requires no mathematics beyond the obligations already listed there. The étale
  formulation is not obtained from it: representing
  \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\) replaces \cref{def:inst_has_pic_scheme} rather than
  supplying its hypothesis, so it needs a representability theorem for a different
  functor. That one formulation is nearer to hand is not an argument that it is the
  right claim to make.
\end{remark}

\begin{theorem}[The Picard identity component is a Jacobian witness]
  \label{def:picardJacobianWitness}
  \uses{def:JacobianWitness, def:genus, thm:fga_pic_representability,
    thm:pic0_isAbelianVariety, thm:pic_zero_dimension_equals_genus,
    thm:albanese_universal_property_northstar}
  \lean{AlgebraicGeometry.picardJacobianWitness}
  The identity component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\) carries a Jacobian witness for
  \(C\).
\end{theorem}
